title: SQL Injection in VulnerableAppointmentRepository.findByStatus
description: The findByStatus method uses template string interpolation to directly embed the status parameter into the SQL query. An attacker can inject SQL by providing a malicious status like 'PENDING' OR '1'='1' -- to bypass the status filter and retrieve appointments of all statuses.
impact: Cross-status appointment data exfiltration. An attacker can retrieve appointments of all statuses (PENDING, CONFIRMED, COMPLETED, CANCELLED) by injecting SQL in the status parameter.
mitigation: Replace template string interpolation with parameterized queries using $1 placeholder for the status parameter.

history.details: Initial audit finding recorded for SQL injection in findByStatus method

Determined status as VALID because Confirmed SQL injection in findByStatus method at line 46: template string with direct interpolation of user-supplied 'status' parameter into SQL query. Test confirms exploitability via sql-injection.test.ts lines 77-142 showing successful injection returning CONFIRMED appointments when querying for PENDING status.

Determined production viability as SAMPLE_OR_TEST because KB freshness gate passes (KB_SNAPSHOT: snap_20250829_01 == active SNAPSHOT_ID: snap_20250829_01). Threat model declares Intent: SAMPLE_OR_TEST_ONLY - this is an educational Security Lab with intentionally vulnerable API (api-vulnerable) for training. All findings reside in intentionally vulnerable demo code, not production deployable artifacts.
Calculated risk score as 3.2 and priority as MEDIUM.
